scene_timeline.dialogue_description: During this intense exchange, Remigio Cardenas, accused of murdering Armando Badajoz, confesses to the crime during his interrogation. When confronted about his guilt, he claims he did not kill Badajoz but instead confessed to stabbing Pastor Emilio, revealing his deep involvement in the chaos surrounding the church. His admission shocks those present, as it directly implicates the pastor in the violence. Remigio’s insistence on his lawyer, Julio Clámez, highlights his desperation and the potential for legal maneuvering. Meanwhile, Speaker 08, likely Emilio, delivers a powerful monologue reflecting on faith and abandonment, drawing parallels between his current suffering and Jesus’ crucifixion. He expresses his belief that through faithfulness, he will rise again, symbolizing both personal and spiritual renewal. His declaration of loyalty to God, despite feeling forsaken, underscores his internal struggle and resolve. The exchange ends with multiple voices chanting "Amen," signifying a shared recognition of the gravity of the moment and the hope for redemption.
